rivers.name: Ganga
rivers.summary: A review compiles fish records across the upper, middle and lower Ganga zones, while ICAR-CIFRI documents riverine germplasm used in restoration.
rivers.scope: Ganga River zones in a literature review; these compiled records are not a current survey.

rivers.name: Brahmaputra
rivers.summary: The upper drainage supports small freshwater fishes as well as the life of the main river. A DNA-barcoding study sampled Siang and Dibang tributaries; this does not imply that every tributary shares the same fauna.
rivers.scope: Siang and Dibang tributaries, East Siang and Lower Dibang Valley, Arunachal Pradesh; five sampled localities.

rivers.name: Cauvery
rivers.summary: A sanctuary survey documents basin-endemic fishes alongside introduced species. Being native to India does not establish native status in the Cauvery.
rivers.scope: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary, Karnataka; survey observations from 2015–2019.

rivers.name: Krishna
rivers.summary: Catfish surveys reveal diversity that can be overlooked in familiar river landscapes. This reference covers a studied Maharashtra stretch, rather than the entire basin.
rivers.scope: Krishna River, Sangli region, Maharashtra; surveys from June 2009–July 2012 and 2013–2017.

rivers.name: Godavari
rivers.summary: Published records span Manjeera and Wardha sub-basin streams, the Godavari description of Rita bakalu, and a single Corica soborna record from the Pranahita sub-basin.
rivers.scope: Manjeera and Wardha sub-basin streams and a Pranahita stream near Talai Village, Telangana; records remain locality-specific.

species.summary: An indigenous Gangetic carp represented in ICAR-CIFRI’s riverine germplasm programme.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Nepal.

associations.note: The source supports indigenous status in the Ganga; it does not support assigning Rohu as native to every Indian river.

species.summary: One of four commercially significant carps selected for the Ganga germplasm programme.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand and south-western China; reported as introduced to China.

associations.note: River ranching is a conservation intervention, not evidence that the species naturally occurs in every reach.

species.summary: The survey identifies the hump-backed mahseer and distinguishes it from unresolved mahseer morphotypes.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.note: Reported as endemic to the Cauvery system. No present-day Red List category is inferred from this 2021 paper.

species.summary: A barb listed among the Cauvery-system endemics in the sanctuary survey.

facts.distribution: Asia: Cauvery basin in India.

associations.note: The basin-endemic designation describes range, not abundance throughout the river.

species.summary: A carp documented among the survey’s Cauvery-system endemics.

facts.distribution: Asia: Cauvery river system in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, India.

associations.note: The record is limited to the study area; the guide does not infer a surveyed underwater scene.

species.summary: A catfish included among the Cauvery-system endemics.

facts.distribution: Asia: Cauvery river drainage in southern India.

associations.note: Locality is intentionally coarse. Historical threat assessments are not displayed as current status.

species.summary: A sisorid catfish for which the Krishna study reports a range extension.

facts.distribution: Asia: Mula Mutha river at Pune, Maharashtra, India.

associations.note: The paper describes an endemic Indian fish; this guide does not claim it is endemic to the Krishna basin.

species.summary: A freshwater fish recorded in tributary streams of the Godavari basin.

facts.distribution: Asia: Ganges River drainage in India, Bangladesh and Nepal, from Himachal Pradesh (Yamuna River) to the estuary; also the Mahanadi drainage and Assam lowlands near the Brahmaputra.

associations.note: Occurrence is documented. This record alone does not resolve whether the Godavari populations are native or introduced.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.locality: Upper Brahmaputra drainage, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh
associations.evidencePeriod: Catalog distribution reviewed 2026-10-23; no observation date stated
associations.note: A regional natural-range summary, not evidence of ubiquitous main-channel occurrence. No microhabitat or basin-endemic claim is made.

facts.distribution: Asia: Cauvery and its tributaries across Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.

associations.note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.

facts.distribution: Asia: endemic to India.

associations.note: The cited survey establishes a historical record and reports basin endemism; it does not establish present abundance, a current threat category or a specific microhabitat.

species.summary: FishBase records Silonia childreni as a demersal, potamodromous freshwater catfish; the Cauvery sanctuary inventory also records the species.

facts.distribution: Asia: Krishna, Godavari and Cauvery river systems in the Western Ghats of peninsular India.

associations.note: The survey table uses a dagger to mark non-native (transplanted or introduced) taxa; this row is unmarked. The record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: FishBase lists the red-tipped halfbeak from Kerala and across marine, brackish and freshwater environments; it also appears in the Cauvery sanctuary inventory.

facts.distribution: Western Indian Ocean: Kerala, India.

associations.note: The survey table uses a dagger to mark non-native (transplanted or introduced) taxa; this row is unmarked. The record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: FishBase describes Wallago attu as a large, elongated freshwater and brackish-water catfish; the Cauvery survey records it in the sanctuary.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan to Viet Nam and Indonesia; also reported from Afghanistan.

associations.note: The survey table uses a dagger to mark non-native (transplanted or introduced) taxa; this row is unmarked. The record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: The Cauvery survey names Opsarius gatensis as a Western Ghats endemic. FishBase describes it from clear hill streams with gravelly or rocky bottoms.

facts.distribution: Asia: Western Ghats, India.

associations.note: The survey marks this species as endemic to the Western Ghats, not to the Cauvery basin. Its sanctuary record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: FishBase places Channa pseudomarulius in the southern Western Ghats and lists it as Not Evaluated; the Cauvery survey marks it as a Western Ghats endemic.

facts.distribution: Asia: Southern Western Ghats, peninsular India.

associations.note: The survey marks this species as endemic to the Western Ghats, not to the Cauvery basin. Its sanctuary record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: FishBase describes adult Labeo dyocheilus in clear, active currents of large rivers and gives it a broad South Asian range; the Cauvery survey also records the species.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Nepal; also recorded in the Maeklong, Salween, Chao Phraya and Mekong basins.

associations.note: The survey table uses a dagger to mark non-native (transplanted or introduced) taxa; this row is unmarked. The table does not mark this species as Cauvery-endemic. The record is historical and site-specific.

species.summary: The Cauvery survey’s figure caption calls Macrognathus malabaricus the Malabar spiny eel; FishBase describes it from coastal rivers, streams, inundated ponds and paddy fields.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.note: The survey marks this species as endemic to the Western Ghats, not to the Cauvery basin. The record is historical and site-specific, not evidence of current abundance or presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: FishBase reports the spotted ricefish from eastern India and Bangladesh and notes fresh and brackish coastal habitats; the Cauvery survey records it at the sanctuary, but its native status there is unresolved.

facts.distribution: Asia: eastern India and Bangladesh.

associations.note: The survey records this species at the sanctuary, while the FishBase distribution summary available here gives eastern India and Bangladesh. Occurrence is documented, but the cited records do not settle native origin in the Cauvery.

species.summary: The Sangli survey lists this Endangered, Western Ghats-endemic fish as Bangana nukta; FishBase currently records the name Schismatorhynchos nukta.

facts.distribution: Asia: Maharashtra and Karnataka, India.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The paper's table names this taxon Bangana nukta and marks it Western Ghats-endemic, but not Krishna River-endemic. FishBase currently uses Schismatorhynchos nukta; its taxonomy follows Fricke et al. (2020) separately from the paper's 2013–2017 occurrence record.

species.summary: The Sangli survey recorded zebra loaches as abundant and marked them endemic to both the Western Ghats and Krishna River system; FishBase associates the species with clear mountain streams.

facts.distribution: Asia: Western Ghats and Maharashtra, India.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The Sangli survey marks Botia striata as endemic to the Western Ghats and Krishna River system. It recorded the species at Bahe, Borgaon and Islampur; the record is limited to the studied reach, not the whole basin.

species.summary: FishBase describes the mussullah barb as a potamodromous freshwater fish of clear, fast-flowing upland rivers; the Sangli survey records it in the Krishna reach and lists it as Endangered.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The survey marks this species as Western Ghats-endemic, not Krishna River-endemic. The paper also reports collecting it near Bahe; this dated, site-specific record does not establish current abundance throughout the basin.

species.summary: The Sangli survey records Labeo potail near Palus and Sangli and reports declining numbers in the study reach; FishBase lists the species as Endangered.

facts.distribution: Asia: Maharashtra, the Deccan and the Cauvery river system in India.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The Sangli survey marks this species as Western Ghats-endemic, not Krishna River-endemic. It reports records near Palus and Sangli and concerns about declining numbers in the study area; this does not quantify a present population.

species.summary: The Sangli survey records this rare, Western Ghats-endemic minnow in the Krishna reach; FishBase reports a maximum recorded length of 3.8 cm and a Vulnerable assessment.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The survey marks this species as Western Ghats-endemic, not Krishna River-endemic. Its presence is documented in the dated Sangli study, which does not establish current abundance throughout the basin.

species.summary: The Sangli survey marks Garra bicornuta as endemic to both the Western Ghats and Krishna River system; FishBase records it from the Thunga system and Kolhapur, Maharashtra.

facts.distribution: Asia: Thunga river system in Karnataka and Kolhapur in Maharashtra.

associations.locality: Krishna River, Sangli District, Maharashtra; five-site study reach
associations.note: The Sangli survey marks Garra bicornuta as endemic to the Western Ghats and Krishna River system. This association is limited to the studied reach, not evidence of presence throughout the basin.

species.summary: The Ganga review records golden mahseer in upper-zone reaches. FishBase describes a large, potamodromous Himalayan fish and lists it as Endangered.

facts.distribution: Asia: Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Myanmar.

associations.locality: Ganga River, upper-zone reaches in the review's zonal table
associations.note: Table 5 lists Tor putitora in upper Ganga zones. The review compiles historical distribution records rather than a new survey, and this zonal listing does not establish present abundance throughout the river.

species.summary: FishBase describes Garua bachcha from large freshwater and tidal rivers; the Ganga review lists it in middle- and lower-zone reaches.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan, India, Bangladesh and Nepal.

associations.locality: Ganga River, middle- and lower-zone reaches in the review's zonal table
associations.note: Table 5 lists Clupisoma garua in middle and lower zones and marks a new zonal distribution record. This is a literature compilation, not a contemporary basin-wide survey.

species.summary: Described from the upper Brahmaputra basin in Arunachal Pradesh, Garra arupi was also included among the fishes sampled from Brahmaputra tributaries in a DNA-barcoding study; FishBase lists it as Not Evaluated.

facts.distribution: Asia: upper Brahmaputra basin in Arunachal Pradesh, India.

associations.locality: Siang–Dibang tributary study area, East Siang and Lower Dibang Valley, Arunachal Pradesh; species-level stream not specified
associations.evidencePeriod: Sampled in the 2019 study; collection dates not stated
associations.note: The survey includes Garra arupi among fish sampled across five localities in the Siang–Dibang study area, but does not identify a stream-level site for this species. FishBase gives its distribution as the upper Brahmaputra basin; the entry is not marked basin-endemic because the cited records do not establish its full range.

species.summary: The widespread zig-zag eel is recorded in a DNA-barcoding survey of Brahmaputra tributaries. FishBase describes it from freshwater and brackish habitats and lists it as Least Concern.

facts.distribution: Asia: Pakistan to Viet Nam and Indonesia.

associations.locality: Siang–Dibang tributary study area, East Siang and Lower Dibang Valley, Arunachal Pradesh; species-level stream not specified
associations.evidencePeriod: Sampled in the 2019 study; collection dates not stated
associations.note: The survey includes this species among fish sampled across five localities in the Siang–Dibang study area, but does not identify a stream-level site for this species. FishBase records a broad South and Southeast Asian range; this dated study record does not establish present abundance throughout the Brahmaputra basin.

species.summary: Rita bakalu was described as a new species from the Godavari river system. FishBase reports a maximum recorded length of 11.1 cm standard length and a Data Deficient assessment.

facts.distribution: Asia: India.

associations.evidencePeriod: Description published 2017; collection dates not stated in the abstract
associations.note: The species was described from the Godavari system. The cited description establishes its type-basin record but is not evidence that the species is confined to the Godavari basin. Data Deficient is not equivalent to a low-risk assessment.

species.summary: A 2020 communication reports one Corica soborna specimen from a stream in the Pranahita sub-basin of the Godavari. The first-basin-record paper documents occurrence, not whether the species is native there.

facts.distribution: Asia: India, Indonesia, Brunei and Malaysia; records from Bangladesh and parts of Southeast Asia require confirmation in FishBase.

associations.locality: Stream near Talai Village, Pranahita River sub-basin, Telangana
associations.evidencePeriod: Single-specimen record published 2020; collection date not stated in the abstract
associations.note: The source reports this as the first Godavari-basin record, based on one specimen. Occurrence is documented, but the cited literature does not determine whether the fish is native to the basin.
